comments.story: PDF: Still unfit for human consumption, 20 years later
comments.why: Explains the Xerox scanner compression bug that altered digits in scans.
comments.text: > You may remember that this played a strange role in Obama's birth certificate some years back Just to clarify, the issue with the compression algorithm used by the scanner, not with the PDF format itself. There a few videos of David Kriesel explaining the bug for the curious: [VIDEO]

comments.author: Terr_
comments.story: OCR For construction documents does not work, we fixed it
comments.why: Covers the JBIG2 scanner bug that silently replaced numbers in documents.
comments.text: > OCR for construction documents does not work I'm reminded of the Xerox JBIG2 bug back in ~2013, where certain scan settings could silently replace numbers inside documents, and bad construction-plans were one of the cases that led to it being discovered. [0] It wasn't overt OCR per se , users weren't trying to convert pixels to characters. [0] [VIDEO]

comments.text: Sounds like the next iteration of "Lies, damned lies and scans": [VIDEO] >On the scale of things too horrible to contemplate, "document-altering scanner" is right up there with "flesh-eating bacteria".
